scope_allowed: Relevance of the quantities of interest

models.name: Model E1: Full-order 3D explicit FEA
models.what_it_computes: Detailed conductor-insulation contact with frictional micro-slip using explicit dynamics; local principal strain range in conductor filars, fretting work density at interfaces, and a cycle-by-cycle damage index used to estimate fatigue life.

models.name: Model E2: Layered orthotropic surrogate (explicit)
models.what_it_computes: Axisymmetric-equivalent, multilayer explicit model calibrated to replicate global bending stiffness and local curvature amplification; computes curvature amplitude, strain energy density in conductor-equivalent layers, and hotspot strain ranges.

models.name: Model E3: Beam–spring reduced-order explicit model
models.what_it_computes: Nonlinear Timoshenko beam segments coupled by penalty contact springs to represent conductor-insulation interaction; computes alternating bending strain at geometric discontinuities and curvature waveforms along the lead path.

mechanisms.name: Axillo-subclavian crush bend
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Cyclic compression and lateral shear between the clavicle and first rib can concentrate strain and induce low-cycle conductor fatigue.

mechanisms.name: Tricuspid annulus excursion bend
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Heart motion drives high-cycle, low-amplitude bending across the valve plane, accumulating damage over time.

mechanisms.name: Header strain-relief bend
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Handling-induced curvature near the connector combined with respiration can create persistent hotspots at the transition from the strain-relief to free lead.

mechanisms.name: Pectoral pocket out-of-plane sweep
mechanisms.why_it_matters: Arm elevation and muscle contraction impose multi-axial bending in the generator pocket, potentially activating off-axis fatigue mechanisms.

deviation.detail: All credibility factor results are scored on a 0–5 scale (0=no support, 5=strong support) for each model–mechanism pair, with acceptance defined as mean score ≥4.0 and no factor <3.0; overall model risk is reported as 3.6/5 with rationale.

spans: Geometry was reconstructed from micro-CT of the subject device at 10 µm voxel resolution.

Filar–silicone contact employed a penalty-based friction law with a measured kinetic friction coefficient of 0.45 and static coefficient 0.60 in 0.9% saline; a Stribeck-type transition allowed a velocity-dependent drop in friction from static to kinetic over 0–2 mm/s.
findings.span: Geometry was reconstructed from micro-CT of the subject device at 10 µm voxel resolution.

spans: The method-of-manufactured-solution problems for linear elasticity and explicit dynamics exhibited the expected first-order temporal and near-second-order spatial convergence rates, and errors below 0.6% in energy norms at the production discretization levels.
Analytic beam deflection and helical bending tests agreed within 0.3 mm at key nodes and within 1.0% in energy balance, supporting the correctness of the implemented formulations and scripts.
findings.span: The method-of-manufactured-solution problems for linear elasticity and explicit dynamics exhibited the expected first-order temporal and near-second-order spatial convergence rates, and errors below 0.6% in energy norms at the production discretization levels.

spans: For E1, the change in peak filar surface principal strain range at the hotspot with mesh and time step refinement remained below 3.5% in the crush, tricuspid, and header cases and at 4.8% in the pocket case.
Artificial hourglass energy stayed below 1.5% of internal energy across all mechanisms, and the kinetic-to-internal energy ratio did not exceed 8% at cycle peaks.
findings.span: For E1, the change in peak filar surface principal strain range at the hotspot with mesh and time step refinement remained below 3.5% in the crush, tricuspid, and header cases and at 4.8% in the pocket case.

spans: In the axillo-subclavian crush, predicted cycles to first crack matched observed cycles with a geometric mean ratio of 1.04 across N=12, and 90% of specimens fell within 0.75–1.35 of the model prediction.
Hotspot locations predicted by E1 overlapped early fretting scars identified by micro-CT in 11 of 12 specimens; the remaining specimen had a secondary hotspot within 2 mm of the predicted location.
findings.span: In the axillo-subclavian crush, predicted cycles to first crack matched observed cycles with a geometric mean ratio of 1.04 across N=12, and 90% of specimens fell within 0.75–1.35 of the model prediction.
